claim_decisions.statement: FAO's April 2025 launch summary estimates US$263 million in agricultural recovery needs, including US$95 million prioritized for 2025/26; proposed farm, irrigation and natural-resource restoration is not proven delivery.

pathways.climate_pressure: Pre-existing climate-related water-supply pressure described by the 2025 UN assessment.
pathways.documented_impact: Attacks damaged water facilities and disrupted household supply, including a named Rmeich case.
pathways.fcv_mediator: War-related infrastructure destruction and restricted inspection compound already strained water provision.
pathways.possible_consequence: Reduced household and service capacity to manage water stress, without attributing the conflict or site-specific water losses to climate.
alternative_explanations: Economic crisis, infrastructure maintenance and service governance also shape water access independently of climate or the assessed hostilities.
pathways.uncertainty: Historical 2024-war assessment; source-stated compounding mechanism, not a measured climate-conflict interaction or current 2026 service audit.
resilience_factors: Proposed irrigation and farm recovery are needs and priorities, not evidence of restored capacity.
pathways.compact_statement: War-damaged water facilities in southern Lebanon compound pre-existing climate-related supply pressure and restrict households' coping capacity.

gaps: The new reports assess 2023-2024 hostilities and 2024-2025 recovery, not current October 2026 damage or service conditions.
The UN water passage places Rmeich in Tyre; this potentially inconsistent district label was not accepted as a verified site-to-district mapping.

executive_assessment.text: Named agricultural damage and Rmeich water disruption show historical conflict-related losses that intersect with existing climate stress; municipal sampling and inspection gaps limit coverage.
War-related ecosystem damage and institutional weakness constrain resilience; heat projections and recovery needs remain scenario-limited or unevaluated.
